question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

By the skin of your teeth
solution:
The correct answer is: **Just barely **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**By the skin of your teeth**" is an idiom that means "just barely" or "narrowly avoiding something." (बस बमुश्किल या बाल-बाल बचे किसी चीज़ से बचना)
 
• This phrase is often used to describe a situation where someone barely escapes danger or failure.
 
 
• **For example**: *He passed the exam by the skin of his teeth, with just one point above the passing mark.*
 
 
 
• The origin of this idiom is uncertain, but it may come from the Bible or from ancient Greek mythology.
 
• Grammatically, this phrase is a prepositional phrase consisting of the preposition "by," the noun "skin," and the prepositional phrase "of your teeth."

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Confident of victory**," is not the correct meaning of this idiom. It is the opposite of the actual meaning.
 
• "**Kind towards the weak**," is not related to this idiom at all.
 
• "**Determined to strike**," is also not related to this idiom. It suggests a different kind of situation entirely.
